rich_narrative.summary: Intercultural Networks, Inc. (ING) is a long-standing organization focused on <cite id="1">promoting understanding and countering bigotry</cite> through education and interfaith engagement. founded in 1993, the organization has spent over three decades <cite id="2">providing interfaith panels and educator resources</cite> across the United States. While the mission addresses critical social challenges, the organization's financial structure presents significant concerns for donors. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="3">total revenue of $688,262</cite>, continuing a steady growth trend with a <cite id="4">3-year CAGR of 10.7%</cite>. However, the primary limiting factor is the <cite id="5">program expense ratio of 39.5%</cite>, which is substantially below the <cite id="6">industry standard of 75%</cite> and the <cite id="7">peer median of 90.9%</cite>. This indicates that less than forty cents of every dollar donated is spent directly on program activities. Despite these financial efficiency gaps, the organization maintains <cite id="8">high fundraising efficiency</cite>, spending $0.00 to raise every $1. Its operational reach remains consistent, with reports indicating it <cite id="9">reached 25,540 people</cite> and served <cite id="10">469 different groups</cite> through its various training and dialogue initiatives.
